definition: Infrared radiation that every object gives out because of its temperature; it needs no medium, so it can travel through a vacuum.
A surface that gives out infrared radiation; at the same temperature, a dull black surface is the best emitter and a shiny white or silvery one the worst.
A surface that takes in the infrared radiation falling on it; dull black surfaces are the best absorbers, while shiny white or silvery surfaces absorb least and reflect most.
A space with no particles of matter in it; radiation can travel through a vacuum, but conduction, convection and sound cannot.
The warming of the Earth's surface because greenhouse gases in the atmosphere, such as carbon dioxide, absorb some of the infrared the surface emits and send some back towards it.
